messages:
nina-sales: Hey team — customer (FinRegCo) wants to run a 2-week POC. Requirements: all inference for EU and APAC tenants MUST stay in-region (no US egress), and they require no US-based subprocessors for model hosting. Also asking what a pricing uplift looks like if we pin a tenant to two regions concurrently. Any blockers?

sam-se: quick clarifying Q — do they want active-active in EU+APAC (traffic split) or active-primary EU with APAC failover?

nina-sales: Active-active, roughly 60/40 traffic split. Low latency required for both. They also sent a security addendum asking for subprocessor attestation and certs.

luis-ops: We can do region-affinity for tenant routing using a customer-zone pin. Two options: (1) Hosted with reserved Dedicated capacity in each region (we pin tenant to RGs in eu-west & ap-southeast), or (2) Private deployment (VPC) in customer's cloud. Hosted Dedicated is faster.

luis-ops: Caveats: - Cross-region control-plane metadata flows may hit US unless we do private control plane. - KMS: if they need BYOK with regional keys, we support GCP/AKV/AWS regional KMS but key storage must be in-region. - Subprocessor list: model infra in eu/apac is fine but some 3rd-party observability/export endpoints live in US by default; we can disable exports.

anya-legal: For the security addendum they asked for granular subprocessor certs (SOC2 + ISO27001 + up-to-date cert chain). We need to produce: signed subproc list, location mapping (which region each subproc operates in), and a statement on control-plane data flows. Legal will need 48h to assemble.

nina-sales: Is there a config snippet I can share to show how routing would be pinned?

luis-ops: Yep — example for the POC (Hosted Dedicated):

```
tenant_routing: 
  strategy: region-affinity
  regions: ["eu-central-1", "ap-southeast-1"]
  mode: active-active
  failover: none
  kms: { region: "eu-central-1", enforce_byo: true }
```

luis-ops: That enforces inference execution in the listed regions. Note: control-plane audit logs still surface to our central logging unless we opt to disable/route them to customer's sink (configurable).

nina-sales: Great. Pricing? what's the uplift for pinned capacity across two regions vs single region Dedicated?

luis-ops: Rough rule: base dedicated commit per region. Two-region active-active ≈ sum of committed capacity for each region + 10-15% overhead for cross-region redundancy and hot-standby buffers. I can get a ballpark number once you give target RPS and model family (quantized vs fp16 matters).

karen-cust-success: I'll gather their expected QPS and model type today and drop it here. Also will ask if they truly need active-active or if active-primary with geo-failover is acceptable (much cheaper). :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Subprocessor inventory v2026-03-18 published: https://internal.redwood/subproc/inventory — note: telemetry/exporter endpoints flagged as US by default.

anya-legal: Action: Legal will prepare subproc attestation + control-plane statement (48h). Ops to confirm whether we can fully eliminate US egress for control-plane (72h). Sales to confirm traffic split and QPS (today).

sam-se: FYI — if customer accepts Private deployment (control-plane in-region + VPC), we can guarantee zero US egress (including control-plane). Cost & lead time higher, but stronger assurance for audits.

nina-sales: Perfect. I'll coordinate with the customer and update by EOD. Thanks all. :pray:

karen-cust-success: Ping me once you have QPS, I'll prep the pricing spreadsheet and a 2-region vs 1-region scenario comparison.

luis-ops: Noted. If we go Hosted Dedicated, ops will need a pre-POC runbook: capacity reservation window, cert-of-isolation checklist, and KMS key provisioning steps. I can draft that once QPS/model are known.

nina-sales: Excellent — moving to action items.
